findings.locator: 7.28.4–45, Durgama request and Brahmā assent paragraph
findings.notes: Request comprises all Vedic mantras with gods/Brahmins in three worlds and strength to conquer gods. Brahmā assents. No death immunity, weapon exception or boon expiration is stated. Null restriction/duration are appropriate witness-scope unknowns.
Brahmins forget Vedas, then bathing/sandhyā/homa/śrāddha/sacrifice/japa cease. Lack of havis progressively weakens gods; Durgama invests Amarāvatī, gods flee to Sumeru caves.
findings.gap_or_recommendation: Prefer explicit wording “Brahmins forget Vedas; rites cease” rather than only “forget Vedic rites”, which compresses epistemic loss into consequence.

findings.notes: Hosted account explicitly relates lost Homa to absent rain; drought lasts100years and kills humans/livestock. Fasted Himalayan prayer follows catastrophe. No inference that100years is tapas duration.

Goddess creates innumerable eyes, appears four-handed with arrows/lotus/bow/plant foods. Many eyes are not narrated biological children; Śatākṣī is their naming response. Translator fourth-dimension gloss excluded properly.

findings.locator: 7.28.4–45 final tears/prayer paragraphs;46–68 opening food distribution
findings.notes: Nine nights are continuous rain from tears, filling rivers. Gods leave caves and with Brahmins request food and Vedas. Thereafter food from the hand and further juicy provisions for humans/grass for beasts are given until crops arise. Śākambharī designation follows nourishment; army encounter follows messengers’ report.
findings.gap_or_recommendation: Nine nights qualify tears/rain, not an exclusive duration for the food provision. Current record preserves that distinction; do not infer festival dates.
